summary: 毛利人按木、骨等材料的特点设计鱼钩。欧洲观察者曾轻视其外形，但博物馆研究与现代延绳钓实践重新肯定了传统钩形的捕捞效果。
logic: 早期评价与后来的研究对照
按猎物和用途变化设计
新材料、仿制品与传统钩形复兴

paragraphs.brief: 毛利人用木头、骨头、石块和松绑制成的鱼钩，其设计和功能尽可能好。
sentences: Maori fish hooks, made from wood, bone, stone and flax, are intended to have the best possible design and function.
毛利人用木头、骨头、石块和松绑制成的鱼钩，其设计和功能尽可能好。
The hooks are designed to target specific species with precision.
钩子的设计是精确地针对特定物种。
In the industry of commercial long-line fishing, there are some Maori hook designs that are making a splash.
在商业延绳钓捕鱼业中，有一些毛利人钩子设计正在喷洒。

paragraphs.brief: 当波利尼西亚人在1100到1300年之间首次来到新西兰时，他们没有必要的技术来熔化和操纵矿石中的金属。
sentences: When Polynesians first came to New Zealand sometime between AD 1100–1300, they didn’t have the technology necessary to melt and manipulate metal from ore.
当波利尼西亚人在1100到1300年之间首次来到新西兰时，他们没有必要的技术来熔化和操纵矿石中的金属。
Meanwhile, fish were the settlers’ main food source, so fishermen made their hooks and fishing gear out of wood, bone, stone and shells.
同时，鱼是定居者的主要食物来源，因此渔民用木头、骨头、石头和贝壳做钩子和渔具。

Other plants native to New Zealand, such as flax (harakeke), cabbage tree (ti), and astelia (kiekie), provided the necessary fibrous material to make fishing-lines and nets of greater or equal strength to the jute used by Europeans at the time.
新西兰本土的其他植物，如麻风(harakeke)、卷心菜树(ti)和白鲸(kikie)，提供了必要的纤维材料，使捕鱼线和网的强度与欧洲人当时使用的黄麻具有较大或同等的强度。

Metal is more malleable and can be shaped in various ways, whereas natural materials are limited in the forms they can take; the Maori fish hooks needed to be innovative in overcoming these limitations.
金属更易于变形，可以不同方式形成，而天然材料的形式则有限；毛利鱼钩需要创新，以克服这些限制。

paragraphs.brief: 定居和探索新西兰的早期欧洲探险家声称，被称为 " matau " 的毛利钩子是 " 奇怪的 "、" 令人怀疑的效力 "、“非常笨拙的事情 " 或 " 不可能看得见 "。
sentences: Early European explorers who settled and explored New Zealand claimed that Maori hooks, known as matau, were “odd”, “of doubtful efficacy”, “very clumsy affairs”, or “impossible looking”.
定居和探索新西兰的早期欧洲探险家声称，被称为 " matau " 的毛利钩子是 " 奇怪的 "、" 令人怀疑的效力 "、“非常笨拙的事情 " 或 " 不可能看得见 "。

Archaeologists from recent times have also described the round hook as odd, with comments such as “shaped in a manner which makes it very difficult to imagine could ever be effective in catching a fish”.
近代的考古学家也把圆钩形容为奇特，他们的评论有“形状很难想象能够有效地捕获鱼”。

William Anderson, who was aboard the Resolution during Cook’s third voyage in 1777 as the ship’s surgeon, remarked that the Maori “live chiefly by fishing, making use … of wooden fish hooks pointed with bone, but so oddly made that a stranger is at a loss to know how they can answer such a purpose.”
1777年库克第三次航行时，曾登上决议的威廉·安德森作为该船的外科医生说，毛利人“主要靠捕鱼生活，使用木钩与骨头对着，但奇怪的是，一个陌生人不知如何应对这个目的。

paragraphs.brief: 新西兰博物馆Te Papa Tongrewa在230年后对毛利鱼钩进行了研究，并表明独特的钩子设计是功能问题。
sentences: The Museum of New Zealand Te Papa Tongarewa conducted a study on Maori fish hooks 230 years later and demonstrated that the unique hook design was a matter of function.
新西兰博物馆Te Papa Tongrewa在230年后对毛利鱼钩进行了研究，并表明独特的钩子设计是功能问题。

The hook’s design allowed it to catch fish by spinning away from the direction of the point and catching their jaws, instead of poking a hole through the fish or being used as a lever, as some archaeologists had suggested.
钩子的设计允许它通过从点的方向旋转和上下巴来捕获鱼，而不是像一些考古学家所说的那样，在鱼中插入一个洞或被用作杠杆。
It appears that the design of the Maori fish hook is perhaps the world’s most efficiently and masterfully designed, likely superior to any modern metal fish hook today.
毛利鱼钩的设计或许是世界上最有效率和最有艺术性的设计，可能优于当今任何现代金属鱼钩。

paragraphs.brief: 为了制造更大的钩子，毛利人用坚固的木头做成的叉子，用骨头或贝壳做尖点。
sentences: To make larger hooks, Maori used shanks made of strong wood, with stout points made of bone or shell.
为了制造更大的钩子，毛利人用坚固的木头做成的叉子，用骨头或贝壳做尖点。
They tied tree branches and saplings together to grow them into ideal shapes for building, then harvested the plants when they reached the appropriate size.
他们把树枝和树苗绑在一起把它们培育成理想的形状用来建造，然后当植物达到适当尺寸时就收获。
They hardened wood by carefully drying it and burying it underground with fires lit above.
他们仔细地将木头干涸，然后用上面点燃的火将木头埋在地下。
Human bone was often used for bone points, which were securely lashed to a groove at the end of the shank using pre-made flax materials (muka).
人体骨骼经常被用于骨点，在腿部末端用预先制成的麻痹材料(muka)将骨头牢牢地压到槽口。
When they wanted to catch larger species like sharks, groper and ling, they used composite hooks.
当他们想捕捉大鱼类时，比如鲨鱼、杂草和，他们用复合钩子。
However, on average, the traditional hook was usually no longer than a three-finger breadth (128 mm in length).
然而，平均而言，传统钩子的宽度通常不超过三指(128毫米)。

paragraphs.brief: 为了捕捉海鸟作为食物和羽毛，例如信天翁，岛民使用细钩，这些小钩子可以与鱼的其他钩子区别开来，因为它们的建造较轻，而且没有转角点。
sentences: To capture seabirds for food and feathers, like albatross, the islanders used slender hooks that can be differentiated from other hooks intended for fish by their lighter build and lack of an in-turned point.
为了捕捉海鸟作为食物和羽毛，例如信天翁，岛民使用细钩，这些小钩子可以与鱼的其他钩子区别开来，因为它们的建造较轻，而且没有转角点。
Many of these hooks were collected by early explorers, suggesting that seabird catching with hook and line was an important source of food and feathers for the Maori (105 mm in length).
早期探险者收集了许多鱼钩，表明用钩子和绳子捕获海鸟是毛利人食物和羽毛的重要来源(长度105毫米)。
Slender hooks with wide gaps were used to capture albatross and other seabirds and can be distinguished from fish hooks by their lighter construction and absence of an in-turned point.
使用缺口大的细钩捕捉信天翁和其他海鸟，可以通过建造较轻的鱼钩和没有转角点将其与鱼钩区别开来。
Early explorers collected many of these hooks, which could indicate that catching seabirds provided significant amounts of food and feathers for the Maori.
早期探险者收集了许多这些钩子，这可能表明捕获海鸟为毛利人提供了大量食物和羽毛。

paragraphs.brief: 象牙或绿石等奢侈品制作的工具可能一直作为装饰品保存，而今天，刻板的毛利鱼钩是文化复兴的象征。
sentences: The Maori quickly adopted new materials once they became available through European explorers, sealers and whalers who began arriving towards the end of the 1700s.
毛利人在通过欧洲探险家、密封船和捕鲸者获得新材料后，很快采用了新材料，这些材料开始接近1700年代末。
At this point, the Maori were still making their fish hooks but were now using metals and imported materials.
目前，毛利人仍在做鱼钩，但现在却在使用金属和进口材料。
Wooden and flax components of old, abandoned fish hooks decomposed quickly as traditional hooks were discarded in favour of new ones.
废弃旧鱼钩的木质和麻痹成分在传统鱼钩被丢弃后迅速腐烂，而采用新的鱼钩。
Tools made of luxury materials such as ivory or greenstone may have been kept as decorative items, with stylised Maori fish hooks today serving as a symbol of cultural revitalisation.
象牙或绿石等奢侈品制作的工具可能一直作为装饰品保存，而今天，刻板的毛利鱼钩是文化复兴的象征。

paragraphs.brief: 毛利人甚至在新材料出现后仍然继续重新创造传统设计，更喜欢1800年代Pakeha引进的钩形。
sentences: The Maori continued to recreate traditional designs even as new materials became available, preferring hook shapes introduced by Pakeha in the 1800s.
毛利人甚至在新材料出现后仍然继续重新创造传统设计，更喜欢1800年代Pakeha引进的钩形。
By maintaining the tradition of the rotating hook design, they remained connected to an essential part of their cultural heritage.
通过保持轮回钩子设计的传统，它们仍然与文化遗产的重要部分相连。
In the end, however, mass-produced European metal hooks eventually dominated, making it difficult to continue crafting hooks from nails, horseshoes and other metal objects.
然而，最终，大量生产的欧洲金属钩最终占主导地位，使得很难继续从钉子、马蹄铁和其他金属物体中制造钩子。
Eventually, traditional designs fell out of favour.
最后，传统的设计却失去了优势。

paragraphs.brief: 到19世纪末和20世纪初，游客和收藏者对毛利工艺品的需求有所增加，导致制造商生产大量伪造钩子。
sentences: By the late 19th and early 20th centuries, tourist and collector demand for Maori artefacts had grown, leading manufacturers to produce large quantities of forged hooks.
到19世纪末和20世纪初，游客和收藏者对毛利工艺品的需求有所增加，导致制造商生产大量伪造钩子。
These replicas were then traded with both Maori and Europeans as forgeries of the real thing, sometimes directly commissioned by artefact dealers.
这些复制品然后作为真品的伪造品与毛利人和欧洲人进行交易，有时是由艺术品商直接委托进行的。

Fake hooks can be identified by their cheap construction, inconsistent materials, rudimentary lashings, odd or overly elaborate decorative carvings, and the absence of in-turned points or angled grooves used to attach the fishing-line properly.
假钩可以用其廉价的构造、不一致的材料、粗糙的鞭笞、奇特或过于精细的雕刻，以及没有用来适当连接捕鱼线的翻转点或角角槽来辨别。

paragraphs.brief: 在整个历史过程中，matau的演变象征着毛利人如何随着时间的推移适应欧洲的工具、材料和技术。
sentences: The evolution of matau throughout history symbolises how the Maori have adapted to European tools, materials and technology over time.
在整个历史过程中，matau的演变象征着毛利人如何随着时间的推移适应欧洲的工具、材料和技术。

It also reflects how European influence contributed to, rather than completely replaced, traditional Maori skills, as native materials were replaced or complemented by metals and, more recently, artificial materials.
它还反映了欧洲的影响如何促进而不是完全取代传统的毛利技能，因为当地材料被金属取代或补充，最近还被人造材料取代或补充。
Today, commercial long-line fishermen around the world have begun using the circle-hook design—one that is nearly identical in appearance and function to the traditional matau.
今天，世界各地的商业延绳钓渔民已开始使用环钩设计，其外观和功能与传统马图几乎相同。
It appears that the advantages and improved catch-rates of this Maori technology have once again been recognised.
看来，毛利人的这种技术的优势和改进的捕捉率再次得到承认。

items.en: Instruction on how to recognise authentic Maori hooks from counterfeit ones
items.zh: 关于如何识别假冒的毛利钩子的指示
items.why: 仿品常用料不一致、绑缚粗糙、装饰过于繁复；I段列出这些识别真假的具体特征。

items.en: A description of a different type of hooks that are not used to catch fish
items.zh: 描述一种不同种类的鱼钩，不用于捕获鱼
items.why: F段所述细长钩用于捕捉信天翁等海鸟，形状与用来钓鱼的钩不同。

items.en: An acknowledgement that Maori design and craftsmanship are still relevant in the modern world
items.zh: 承认毛利人的设计和工艺在现代世界中仍然具有相关性
items.why: 现代延绳钓渔民使用的圆钩，在形状和功能上几乎与传统毛利鱼钩相同，说明这种设计仍有价值。

items.en: An investigation into how the hooks functioned so effectively
items.zh: 调查钩子是如何有效运行的
items.why: 新西兰博物馆研究鱼钩，证明独特形状与实际功能有关，随后解释鱼钩怎样旋转并扣住鱼颌。

items.en: A description of how modern technology began to dominate and eventually took over from traditional hook construction
items.zh: 描述现代技术如何开始主宰并最终从传统的钩子建造中接管
items.why: 欧洲工厂批量生产的金属钩最后占据市场，手工改造钉子、马蹄铁制作鱼钩的办法难以延续。

items.en: A list of raw materials used to construct hooks
items.zh: 用于建造钩子的原材料清单
items.why: B段直接列出制钩和渔具的材料，包括木、骨、石和贝壳。

items.en: An outline of how different styles of hooks and types of materials were employed to catch larger fish
items.zh: 说明如何使用不同种类的钩子和材料捕捞大鱼
items.why: 对付鲨鱼等大型鱼类时，毛利人改用复合钩；本段也说明木柄、骨尖和绑缚材料怎样组合。

items.en: An account of how the Maori employed new technology and adapted it
items.zh: 说明毛利人如何使用新技术并加以改造
items.why: 毛利人继续自己做鱼钩，同时开始采用进口金属等新材料，显示他们吸收并改造外来技术。

items.en: The early European settlers quickly understood how the Maori fish hook worked.
items.zh: 早期的欧洲定居者很快了解毛利鱼钩是如何工作的。
items.why: 早期航海者说外来人看不出这种古怪鱼钩如何奏效，说明他们并未很快理解其原理。

items.en: The hook works by making a hole and embedding itself in the mouth of the fish.
items.zh: 钩子的作用是把洞塞进鱼的嘴里
items.why: 这种钩靠旋转勾住鱼颌，并不会像题干说的那样先刺穿鱼嘴。

items.en: The Maoris catch seabirds by their feet.
items.why: 文中提到用钩捕海鸟以取得食物和羽毛，没有说明钩住的是海鸟的脚。

items.en: There used to be a demand for Maori fish hooks and many counterfeit ones were produced.
items.zh: 以前对毛利鱼钩的需求很大，生产了许多假鱼钩。
items.why: 游客和收藏者需求增长，促使制造者生产大量仿冒毛利鱼钩。

items.en: Today European-style hooks have completely replaced the traditional styles used by the Maoris.
items.zh: 今天，欧洲式钩子完全取代了毛利人使用的传统风格。
items.why: 现代延绳钓仍采用外观和功能都接近传统毛利鱼钩的圆钩，谈不上完全取代。

points: 新西兰博物馆研究鱼钩，证明独特形状与实际功能有关，随后解释鱼钩怎样旋转并扣住鱼颌。
文中提到用钩捕海鸟以取得食物和羽毛，没有说明钩住的是海鸟的脚。
clauses: Early European explorers … claimed that Maori hooks, known as matau, were “odd”, “of doubtful efficacy”, “very clumsy affairs”, or “impossible looking”.
“who settled and explored New Zealand”修饰前面的 explorers。先认出先行词，再读从句补充的特征。
读到 who 时，回看 explorers，再把修饰信息接回主句。

William Anderson, who was aboard the Resolution during Cook’s third voyage in 1777 as the ship’s surgeon, remarked that the Maori “live chiefly by fishing, making use … of wooden fish hooks pointed with bone, but so oddly made ….”
“that a stranger is at a loss to know how they can answer such a purpose”补足 made 的内容，交代究竟在说、判断或发现什么。
先读 made 所在的主句，再把 that 后面的内容作为一个整体。
